title: Tech Note: Localizing the Textual Representation of Numbers in Various Languages Using STRtoArray
author: Kent Wilbur
featured_technology: Multi-language currency/number-to-words conversion (English, French, German, Spanish)

historical_commentary.text: This note shows how to localize the textual (spelled-out) representation of numbers and currency amounts (e.g. "one hundred dollars") across English, French, German, and Spanish, comparing a hard-coded-array approach against a more maintainable approach using STR# Macintosh resources loaded at runtime via ACI_PACK's STRtoArray external; the specific mechanism (STR# resources edited with ResEdit/Resorcerer, ACI_PACK) is entirely obsolete classic-Mac-OS tooling, but the general problem of localizing number/currency spelling into multiple languages remains a real, still-relevant software localization concern, now typically solved with dedicated i18n libraries rather than resource forks.
related_updates: ACI_PACK, STR# resources, and ResEdit/Resorcerer are all classic Mac OS-era tools with no equivalent in current 4D or modern operating systems

Modern number/currency localization (including spelled-out text representations) is typically handled via dedicated internationalization (i18n) libraries or platform locale APIs rather than resource-fork-based string tables
4D's own plugin/resource architecture has been substantially modernized since 1996, removing the need for Mac-resource-fork-based localization data
